headline: High: shared server datastore and broad egress create default risks of data leakage and cascading misuse between Flowise and RD-Agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write files and run browser/tool nodes, while RD-Agent can ingest logs/files and browser/API outputs. A shared server datastore plus file-based handoff makes prompt injection plausible if one agent consumes the other's generated content as instructions. The pathway is documented by both profiles, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF Flowise outputs are written into a shared workspace that RD-Agent later parses as instructions
IF RD-Agent ingests Flowise-generated files or logs without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent files
Disable automatic instruction parsing from shared files
Review browser/tool outputs before reuse
requires-engineering: enforce content-type allowlists

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, and RD-Agent touches financial reports, research data, execution traces, and logs while calling third-party APIs. If they share storage or credentials, sensitive data can flow from one agent into the other's outputs or external API calls by default. The pairwise leakage path is supported by both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or datastore
IF either agent forwards shared files or logs to external model APIs
mitigations: Use separate encrypted workspaces
Rotate and scope API keys per agent
Block sensitive files from API-bound tools
Audit logs for cross-agent data flow
requires-engineering: add DLP filters before egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has filesystem write access and broad network egress; RD-Agent has API access and writes logs. Even without explicit git or DB writes, overlapping mutable surfaces can conflict if both operate on the same directory or shared datastore. Uncertainty about deployment isolation pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore
IF orchestration does not provide locking or per-agent namespaces
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Enable file locking in the orchestrator
Make one agent read-only on shared artifacts
Schedule non-overlapping runs
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise can generate tool outputs and RD-Agent can consume logs, papers, and traces for downstream research actions. If RD-Agent treats Flowise-produced content as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect analyses or API-driven actions. Both profiles support the pathway, but there is no direct evidence of automatic trust.
conditions: IF RD-Agent uses Flowise outputs as inputs without validation
IF Flowise-generated facts are reused in RD-Agent workflows
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require source citations for reused facts
Flag low-confidence outputs for manual review
Limit automated actions to non-destructive steps
requires-engineering: add schema validation

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, while RD-Agent processes financial reports, research papers, competition datasets, and logs. If EU or regulated data is routed through RD-Agent's third-party API calls, retention and residency obligations may diverge from Flowise's handling. The profiles show compliance-relevant data classes but not a documented DPA or residency guarantee.
conditions: IF regulated or EU personal data is placed into either agent's workflows
IF the deployment lacks a DPA or approved residency controls for external API calls
mitigations: Classify data before routing it
Keep regulated data out of external API calls
Document retention settings for both agents
Restrict logs to non-sensitive fields
requires-engineering: add residency enforcement
